summary: @onereach/condition-builder ships a preinstall dropper that fetches the Bun runtime to execute an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package's preinstall lifecycle script (package.json runs `node setup.mjs`) downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<platform>.zip, extracts and chmods the platform binary, and uses it to execute a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB single-line, heavily obfuscated `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle using a rotating string-array decoder and hex-named identifiers, and it is executed only under the freshly-downloaded Bun binary — Node-based tooling never resolves or runs its contents. setup.mjs itself is obfuscated in obfuscator.io style, with string-property indirection maps hiding literals such as `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `bun`, and the Bun download URL. A condition-builder UI library has no legitimate reason to install a second JavaScript runtime at npm install time solely to execute an opaque sibling script. The choice of an alternate runtime bypasses Node-based supply-chain review of the payload, and the obfuscation of both the visible dropper and the executed bundle is inconsistent with legitimate build glue. Installing this package causes arbitrary attacker-controlled code to execute on the installer's machine at `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
